concept.name: Liquidity pool
concept.definition: A liquidity pool is a smart contract holding reserves of two (or more) tokens that an AMM uses as the counterparty for swaps; traders trade against the pooled reserves and liquidity providers fund them in exchange for a share of fees.
concept.intuition: It is a communal vault of token pairs: everyone chips in inventory, the vault quotes prices from its contents, and depositors split the toll every trader pays.
concept.mechanics: Providers deposit proportional amounts of both tokens and receive pool shares (LP tokens in v2, NFT positions in v3) representing their pro-rata claim on reserves plus accrued fees. Swaps move the reserve ratio, repricing the pair via the pool's invariant (e.g. x·y=k), and a per-swap fee (e.g. 0.3%) accrues to the pool.
concept.failure_modes: Pools for scam or exploited tokens can be drained or become worthless, and permissionless listing means anyone can create deceptive pools; thin pools give extreme slippage and are easy to manipulate for oracle attacks.
concept.misconceptions: Pool depth (TVL) is not a guarantee of fair pricing — prices still track external markets only via arbitrage. Depositing into a pool is not like depositing into a savings account; the asset mix you withdraw is usually different from what you put in.
concept.example: A Uniswap ETH/USDC pool holding 10,000 ETH and 40M USDC lets a trader swap 100,000 USDC for ~24.9 ETH instantly; the 0.3% fee (~300 USDC) stays in the pool, enriching all LP shares.
